note: Curated guidance only. Signatures never live here: `contract` entries are pointers into `api --op` output, `proofs` are job names of the lane suite, `negative` are refusal jobs; the index build refuses any pointer that does not resolve. `limits` and `guidance` are text with an `origin` and are labelled guidance in every answer. `depends` entries are mandatory unless they carry `unless` (a condition the caller checks against the capture: the element may already exist); `recommends` are optional; `alternatives` are decisions. `context.kinds` are the reader kinds listed with --app and `context.signatures` the kinds whose matching elements get their signature read. Capabilities shared with the O11 lane (data.static, data.structure) live in discovery-capabilities-shared.json and are merged into this lane at index build.

job.operation: kernel job JSON {description, base, expectValid, expectedMessages, ops[]} using the compact ops (spec/logic/screen/html) or the raw verbs (api --op verbs)
job.prove: .\ssam job --lane odc <job.json>  (only when the person asks for a headless proof on the lane fixture; delivers nothing) / MCP ssam_job {lane:"odc", job}
job.deliver: .\odc deliver <feature> --job <job.json> --module <Module> --owners '["Owner"]' --changes '["Change"]'  (directly: captures the open module, validates, previews and merges in one call) / MCP studio_deliver {feature, job, module, owners, changes}

feature.operation: C# feature in platforms/odc/studio/builder/features (IFeature: Name, Module, Transaction, Owners, Changes, Apply, Verify) using the Authoring*.cs primitives

reader.operation: read a capture (.oml) or an open module by name, starting with the module map; identities are bound to sourceSha256
entries: .\ssam map --lane odc <capture.oml|Module> [--kind K] [--name N] [--prefix P] [--role R] [--parent @key] [--offset N] [--max N] (first: every element with its @key)
ssam_map {lane:"odc", target, kind, name, prefix, role, parent, offset, max}
.\odc inspect <capture.oml> [Kind:Name/...|@key] [--kind K] [--name N] [--text T] [--usages] [--select p ...] [--budget N] --expectedSourceSha256 <hash>
studio_inspect {target, path, kind, name, text, select, usages, budget, expectedSourceSha256}

data.operation: the Studio's own data service on the development database, module open
entries: studio_data_insert|update|delete (require the user's own authorization words)

delivery.operation: snapshot -> build/apply -> check-base -> preview -> merge (strictlyEqual) -> authorize -> publish

prototype.operation: ONE studio_deliver call (through the ssam server) with the job op prototype: SSAM captures the prototype headless, builds one native screen per view, the shell block, popups, entities with the mock data and the logic, measures the fidelity on the module read back, merges, publishes and loads the demo data; the receipt is prototype
prototype.deliver: studio_deliver {feature, module, job:{ops:[{op:"prototype", data:{source}}]}, owners, changes, publish:true, authorize}

slots.source: the absolute folder of the prototype (or its .html entry)
slots.module: the module open in ODC Studio
slots.Prefix: the prototype <title> up to the first separator, in PascalCase (FarmaVirtual); feature, owners and changes may be left out: the ssam server fills them from it

rules: Do not read the prototype files and never convert them by hand: SSAM reads them.
One call; the owner's words in authorize cover the import, the publication and the demo data.
data.mapping only when a refusal asks for it: apply its patch as it is (one refusal brings every problem).
Rehearsal without merge only when the person asks: until:"preview" (ODC has no until apply).
Give the person the links of prototype.screens[].url.

capabilities.title: Client entities (local storage) and client-side aggregates
capabilities.summary: `spec.clientEntities` declares local storage entities (Id without AutoNumber); client actions write them with CreateOrUpdate and screen aggregates read them with `args.isClientSide`.

limits.text: Public client entities are not preserved by native merge in this Studio build; expose a public structure instead.

capabilities.title: Read or write records of the development database
capabilities.summary: The Studio's own data service (View data / Edit data) reads and writes records of an entity of the open module; writes need the user's own authorization words. Not a model change.

limits.text: Reading is proven live; inserts/updates/deletes have no receipt in the repository yet (HANDOFF §4: the 'P' items without proof). Corporate tenants only on explicit instruction.

capabilities.guidance: The module must be open in the Studio; there is no public ODC API for business data.

capabilities.title: Settings (site properties), client variables, roles and user exceptions
capabilities.summary: Create ISiteProperty (the product calls it Setting; expressions read `Settings.<Name>`), IClientVariable, IRole and IUserException with the raw verbs; restrict a screen with `link from $scr connector Roles to $role`.

limits.text: On ODC a Setting is read-only inside actions (writing it is an error); IsSecret changes how the value is stored, not the model.

capabilities.guidance: Session variables do not exist on ODC: use a client variable.

capabilities.title: Server action with steps (op logic)
capabilities.summary: Declare inputs/outputs/vars and steps (get, assign, call, save/create/update/delete, if/then/else, foreach, raise); Start/End, links and layout are generated; unknown keys, unresolved names and unused inputs fail before touching the model.

alternatives.when: the action already exists and must keep its consumers

limits.text: On ODC an aggregate Count is Long Integer; a private server action without consumer gets the warning UnusedUserAction (declare it in expectedMessages).
while/switch/break/continue/return/handlers/comments and joins/columns of the logic language are accepted by the compiler but have no ODC job yet (proven on O11 only).
limits.origin: index: no ODC job uses those keys

capabilities.guidance: A screen saves through a server action wrapper (CreateOrUpdate inside it), never by calling the entity action directly (Security warning). Do not name an aggregate `Get<Entity>s`: a filter renames it and expressions break.

capabilities.title: Aggregates: filters, sorts, joins, group by and aggregations
capabilities.summary: In `logic` a `get` step with where/sort/max; a full aggregate with join, group by and aggregated columns is built with the raw verbs (IAggregateNode, IAliasedSource, IJoin, IFilter, ISort, IGroupByAttribute, IAggregatedAttribute).

route.operation: logic step {"get":"Entity","as":"GetX","where":"...","sort":[["X.Attr","Ascending"]],"max":50} or verbs on IAggregateNode

alternatives.when: the query cannot be expressed as an aggregate
a screen needs data fetched by logic instead of a screen aggregate

limits.text: ODC names the aggregated column type IAggregatedAttribute (SS11: IAggregateAttribute); Count and Sum are Long Integer.

capabilities.guidance: Without group by read `GetX.List.Current.<Entity>.<Attr>`; with group by or aggregations read `GetX.List.Current.<Column>`.

capabilities.title: SQL query with parameters
capabilities.summary: `get` with `sql:true`, `statement` and `params`; the output is named List: a field reads `<as>.List.Current.List.<Field>`.

alternatives.when: an aggregate can express it (preferred, native filters/joins)

limits.text: where/sort/start are refused with sql:true: filter, sort and page inside the statement; declared params and @names must match.

capabilities.title: Service actions (remote, loosely coupled)
capabilities.summary: `logic` with kind `service` (or raw IServiceAction) exposes logic to other apps; consumers are remote (ReferenceServiceAPIMethod), so zero local usages is normal.

alternatives.when: the caller is in the same module

limits.text: A local IExecuteServerActionNode cannot point at a service action on ODC (Model API refuses); a service action delegates to a private server action. Public and Shareable move together.

capabilities.title: Client actions and JavaScript nodes
capabilities.summary: IClientAction with an IJavaScriptNode (inputs/outputs as parameters) created with the raw verbs; called from a screen action with IExecuteClientActionNode.

route.operation: create IClientAction + IJavaScriptNode; set JavaScript; IExecuteClientActionNode from a screen action

limits.text: The compact `logic` kind client is accepted by the compiler but proven on ODC only through raw verbs; a JavaScript parameter Description is not allowed by the native API.

capabilities.guidance: Prefer native nodes and data actions; use JavaScript only where the request needs the browser.

capabilities.title: Screen actions (button/link/event handlers)
capabilities.summary: A screen action lives in the screen (`create IScreenAction` under `$scr`, or `logic` kind `screen` with `owner`); a button binds with `set $btn/OnClick Destination $action`; navigation to another screen uses `Destination IMobileScreen:X` plus `$btn/OnClick/<Input> Value`.

route.operation: create IScreenAction under the screen; set $btn/OnClick prop Destination

depends.unless: the screen already exists (address it as IMobileScreen:Name; ui.edit)

limits.text: Reactive/Mobile screen actions cannot declare outputs. Button/link clicks and screen lifecycle events use Destination; block instance events use Handler (wrong property costs a delivery cycle).

capabilities.title: Data actions (screen data fetched by logic) and Refresh Data
capabilities.summary: IDataAction created under the screen with an output list, Fetch AtStart|OnDemand, OnAfterFetch Destination to a screen action, and IRefreshDataNode to reload it; the list reads `<DataAction>.<Output>.Current.<Field>`.

route.operation: create IDataAction under $scr; set Fetch; delete $da/Out1; create IOutputParameter; flow nodes; set $da/OnAfterFetch Destination

depends.unless: the screen already exists (create the data action under IMobileScreen:Name)

alternatives.when: the data is a plain entity query: a screen aggregate is simpler

limits.text: On ODC a Data Action cannot declare input parameters (IDataAction has no CreateInputParameter); pass screen state through Refresh Data.
The compact `logic` kind data (with `fetch`) is accepted by the compiler; the ODC proof uses raw verbs.

capabilities.guidance: Idiomatic ODC: initial query by screen aggregate; external/computed data by Data Action + Refresh; submit through a screen action calling a server action.

capabilities.title: Native nodes: Message, Destination, Download, JSON, Excel
capabilities.summary: In `logic` a `node` step names the native node type and its closed properties (api --op logic nativeNodes): IMessageNode, IDestinationNode, IDownloadNode in screen actions; IJSONSerializeNode/IJSONDeserializeNode, IRecordListToExcelNode/IExcelToRecordListNode in server actions.

limits.text: Message and Destination never live in server actions; Download only in screen actions; RecordListToExcel only in server actions (ODC census of 45 real modules).

capabilities.title: Exceptions, handlers and switch
capabilities.summary: Raise a user exception with the `raise` step; ISwitchNode + ISwitchCondition and the global IOnExceptionAction (child of a UI flow, no Start node) are built with the raw verbs; exceptions are renamed/repointed/deleted like any element.

limits.text: Switch requires OtherwiseTarget (InvalidFlow_NoOtherwise); an exception handler has no Start node, so `layout` does not apply (position with move x/y). Do not repoint IESpace.GlobalExceptionHandler on an app that has one (three new warnings).

capabilities.guidance: The compact `handlers` key is accepted by the compiler but unproven on ODC; raw verbs are the proven path.

capabilities.title: Edit an existing action (parameters, nodes in the middle of a flow, rename, repoint)
capabilities.summary: Address the action by `IServerAction:Name` (or IClientAction/IScreenAction), its children by path, an argument by `arg:<Param>`; splice a node by linking its exit first and repointing the predecessor after; use usages before delete and replace to repoint callers.

alternatives.when: rewriting the whole body: `logic` with replace:true keeps consumers (proven on O11; on ODC the raw-verb edits are the proven path)

limits.text: Adding an input to a called action creates an empty argument in every caller; an argument the author filled survives the parameter's deletion as an orphan (UnusedArgument warning).
On ODC `<Node>.<Output>` expressions follow a rename automatically; on O11 they do not. `rename` reports expressionsRewritten 0 in that case on both lanes: read the expressions back.

capabilities.title: Consume a REST API (client, structures, methods, call it)
capabilities.summary: IRestClient with BaseURL, IRestStructure(s) for request/response (nested: child first, then its name as DataType), IRestAction with URLPath (query string inside it, one UrlPlacement input per {param}), inputs/outputs by placement; a server action calls it with IExecuteServerActionNode -> IRestAction:Name.

alternatives.when: the request needs the C# AuthoringRest primitives (RotaSegura pattern)

limits.text: Username/Password exist in the ODC API and accept writes, but Verify rejects them as errors: only the authentication mode stays in the model; credentials live outside it.

capabilities.guidance: Native type names come from the ODC Model API index (discover --detail logic.rest-consume --type IRestAction).

capabilities.title: Expose a REST API
capabilities.summary: IRestService + IRestServiceAction (born with Start/End), inputs in the URL, output typed by a structure, an Assign fills the response.

limits.text: Renaming an exposed method rewrites its URLPath (the public URL changes) while rename reports consumers 0: external consumers are invisible to the model.

capabilities.title: Timers (scheduled server actions)
capabilities.summary: ITimer with Action, Description, CronSchedule/Schedule and TimeoutInMinutes; the schedule tree (ScheduleConfiguration) is derived and rebuilt when the parent property changes.

route.operation: create ITimer; set Action IServerAction:X; set CronSchedule

depends.unless: the server action to schedule already exists (set Action IServerAction:Name)

capabilities.title: Application events, external sites and extended (DOM) events
capabilities.summary: ISystemEvent (OnApplicationReady; empty flow to author), IExternalSite (a UI flow node with an URL input) and IEvent (extended event of a widget bound to a screen action without outputs).

route.operation: create ISystemEvent|IExternalSite|IEvent with the raw verbs

limits.text: The platform refuses `rename` on IEvent and ISystemEvent; an extended event is renamed by writing `Event` (closed list of 11 DOM names).

capabilities.title: Screen with layout, container, expressions, inputs and a button
capabilities.summary: `create IMobileScreen` in `IMobileFlow:MainFlow`, bind the layout instance (`set $scr/#IMobileBlockInstanceWidget SourceBlock IMobileBlock:LayoutTopMenu`), add widgets under the layout placeholders (Title, MainContent, Actions), inputs bound to local variables or aggregate fields, buttons bound to screen actions.

route.operation: raw verbs: create IMobileScreen / IContainer / IExpression / IInput / IButton; set SourceBlock, Variable, Value, Text

alternatives.when: the content is easier to write as an HTML fragment
an archetype (cards/table/detail/form/dashboard) fits and the module references the OutSystemsUI blocks it needs (unproven on ODC)

limits.text: On ODC the layouts (LayoutTopMenu, LayoutBase) are blocks of the module itself; the ESpace is CrossDevice so the mobile vocabulary applies; a button's caption lives inside IContent (`$btn/#ITextWidget`).

capabilities.guidance: Screens created headless become DefaultScreen when the module had none; the first screen may need a different DefaultScreen before deletion (delete-screen).

capabilities.title: Form bound to a record: load by id, edit fields, save
capabilities.summary: Screen input (Id), IScreenAggregate filtered by it, IForm with IInput/ICheckbox bound to `GetX.List.Current.<Entity>.<Attr>`, a Save button whose screen action calls a server action wrapper that runs CreateOrUpdate<Entity>.

route.operation: screen-form.json pattern: wrapper server action + screen + aggregate + IForm + inputs + IScreenAction + set $btn/OnClick Destination

depends.unless: the entity already exists (bind the form to IServerEntity:Name; its attributes are in context.signatures)
a save wrapper action for that entity already exists (call it from the screen action)
the screen already exists (add the form under IMobileScreen:Name/...; ui.edit)

recommends.when: the module already exists: read its entities, screens and referenced blocks (--app) before declaring new ones

alternatives.when: the archetype form (kind form) is acceptable: fields input|textarea|checkbox only, no dropdown field, unproven on ODC

limits.text: Mandatory comes from the attribute or `set Mandatory True`; the screen must not call the entity action directly (wrapper server action).

capabilities.guidance: For a selectable field inside the form combine with ui.dropdown (native, unproven on ODC) or ui.dropdown-search (block, read its contract from the capture).

capabilities.title: List of records with item navigation
capabilities.summary: IScreenAggregate with ISort, IList with Source `GetX.List`, IListItem with expressions in its Content, `set $item/OnClick Destination IMobileScreen:Detail` plus `$item/OnClick/<Input> Value`.

depends.unless: the screen already exists (place the list under IMobileScreen:Name/...)

alternatives.when: the list body is easier as `<div list as>` HTML

limits.text: A ListItem is born with an example swipe action without destination: delete `$item/RightActions/#IListItemAction`. On ODC the children of a List live inside an IContent (paths show IList:X/IContent:content/...).
ITableRecords (table with columns) has no ODC job; it is B (vocabulary) not C.
limits.origin: index: no ODC job creates ITableRecords

capabilities.title: Native dropdown (IDropdown) bound to a list
capabilities.summary: Native IDropdown widget bound to a list source and to a record field of the screen; its property names for this Studio are in the native index (`--type IDropdown`, A) and the visual `html` op maps the `select` tag to it (html-visual.tags, B).

route.operation: create IDropdown under a container; set its properties (names from --type IDropdown) with raw verbs, or `<select>` in html-visual

depends.unless: the screen already exists (place the widget under IMobileScreen:Name/...)

alternatives.when: the user must type to search: the OutSystemsUI DropdownSearch block, not the native widget

limits.text: No ODC job creates an IDropdown: the kernel accepts it (B: verbs + Model API) and it is proven on O11 (gallery-native-reactive.json, widgets-reactive.json); deliver it directly (studio_deliver validates the job on a fresh capture and refuses before any change); a headless proof (ssam_job) only when the person asks for one.
The native dropdown has no search behaviour of its own (O11 vocabulary: DropdownMode Text|Custom; confirm the ODC members with --type IDropdown).
limits.origin: ScreenVocabulary.json (O11 11.55.69) IDropdown; ODC Model API index NRWidgets IDropdown

capabilities.guidance: Property names are not curated here: read them from the native index (discover --detail ui.dropdown --type IDropdown) and from html-visual.tags (select).

capabilities.title: Searchable dropdown (OutSystemsUI DropdownSearch block)
capabilities.summary: An instance of the OutSystemsUI block DropdownSearch referenced by the module. Its inputs, mandatory input types and events (with their parameters) are the signature of the referenced revision: read them from the capture (`--app`: context.signatures, D), never from this text. Instantiate with the visual `html` op (`<Block name="DropdownSearch" :<Input>="expr" @<Event>="ScreenAction">`) or the raw verbs (`create IMobileBlockInstanceWidget` with source `IMobileBlock:DropdownSearch`, `set $b/<Input> Value`, `set $b/<Event> Handler $action`); the handler of the selection event assigns the selection to the record field.

route.operation: html-visual `<Block>` or raw verbs on IMobileBlockInstanceWidget; a screen action builds the option list expected by the block input from an aggregate and another handles the selection event

depends.unless: the screen already exists (place the instance under IMobileScreen:Name/...)
a screen action to handle the mandatory event already exists (set $b/<Event> Handler to it)

alternatives.when: no typing/search is needed: the native IDropdown binds a record field directly

limits.text: No ODC job instantiates DropdownSearch; the nearest ODC proofs are html-visual-block (DatePicker block with input and mandatory handler) and block-events (event handlers). The offline block doc is O11 OutSystemsUI 2.28.1 and is not used by the answer; on ODC the contract is the MobileBlockSignature in the capture (context.signatures with --app, or `odc inspect <capture> "MobileBlockSignature:DropdownSearch" --depth 2`).

A block instance has no Variable of its own: the selected value only reaches the record through the handler of the block's selection event; a mandatory event without handler is a Verify error per instance (EventHandlerRequiredAction).

capabilities.guidance: Build the option list expected by the block input (type in context.signatures) in a screen action or data action from the entity list, keep it in a screen variable, and map the event's selection parameter back to the FK in the handler.

capabilities.title: Reusable block with inputs, placeholders, events and triggers
capabilities.summary: `create IMobileBlock` in a UI flow with IInputParameter, ILocalVariable, IPlaceholderWidget, IBlockEvent (IsMandatory, parameters) fired by an ITriggerNode in a block screen action; instances receive inputs (`set $inst/<Input> Value`) and handlers (`set $inst/<Event> Handler $action`).

limits.text: Changing an event contract breaks the trigger (the producer's arguments mirror the event parameters), not the consumer handlers; the IEventHandler exists even without a handler and counts in usages.
`rename` of an IBlockEvent returns success but writes nothing on ODC in this build: rename its neighbours (trigger node, handler action) instead.

capabilities.guidance: Placeholder content inside the block is example content copied into each instance (owned by the consumer).

capabilities.title: Instantiate an existing block (own or OutSystemsUI) with inputs and handlers
capabilities.summary: Visual `html` op `<Block name="X" :Input="expr" @Event="ScreenAction"><slot name="Placeholder">...</slot></Block>` inside an existing parent, or raw verbs `create IMobileBlockInstanceWidget` with `source`; the block must already be referenced by the module (its signature is readable from the capture).

limits.text: Only the DatePicker OutSystemsUI block has an ODC job; the other patterns (Tabs, Accordion, Search, Pagination, DropdownSearch...) are B on ODC. Placeholders born with an Input are bound with `set .../#IInput Variable`, not `empty`.

capabilities.guidance: List what the module already references: inspect --kind MobileBlockSignature (context.reads).

capabilities.title: HTML/CSS fragment into an existing screen or block (native widgets)
capabilities.summary: The fragment becomes native widgets under an existing parent: div->Container, tags->IAdvancedHtml, text->Text, `{{ expr }}`->Expression, input/select/button/a/label/img, `<div list as>`, `<div if>`, `<Block>`; names must exist in the module; `<style>` is rewritten under the fragment root class.

depends.unless: the parent screen or block already exists (the fragment always needs an existing parent)

alternatives.when: a whole page with bindings manifest (unproven on ODC)

limits.text: Rejected: script, an <i> without weight, names that do not exist, tags outside the table; logic, data and events stay in native verbs.

capabilities.title: Screen archetypes (cards, table, detail, form, dashboard) by op screen
capabilities.summary: One `screen` op declares screens by kind with source (entity or action), search, filters (native dropdown over a static entity), fields/columns/tabs/actions; the compiler composes OutSystemsUI blocks already referenced by the module (Search, Pagination, CardSectioned, Tabs, Gallery/Carousel, Counter).

alternatives.when: the ODC proofs are needed today: raw verbs (screen-form/screen-list) are the proven path

limits.text: Accepted by the compiler for CrossDevice modules but no ODC job runs it (proven on O11: screen-spec-*.json). Form fields are input|textarea|checkbox only (no dropdown field); existing screen names are refused; the referenced OutSystemsUI blocks must exist in the module.

capabilities.guidance: Deliver directly (the deliver call validates and refuses before any change; a headless proof only when the person asks for one); declare the required blocks by reading context.reads MobileBlockSignature.

capabilities.title: Whole page from HTML + bindings manifest (op html data)
capabilities.summary: The page HTML/CSS plus a typed bindings manifest (text, list, field, visible, style, date, navigate, call, refresh) compiled to native widgets, data sources and screen actions; CSS installed in the theme author half.

alternatives.when: the logic stays native and only a fragment is authored (proven on ODC)

limits.text:
No ODC job (proven on O11: html-dashboard-reactive.json). id selectors in CSS are always refused;
, ,

capabilities.title: Edit an existing screen, block or widget (properties, new widgets, reorder, delete)
capabilities.summary: Address by `IMobileScreen:Name/...` or `IMobileBlock:Name/...` and use set (Title, Description, StyleSheet, Style, AnimateItems, argument Values of a block instance), create inside an existing container, move first/last/before/after, delete after usages.

recommends.when: before changing widgets: read the screen subtree (depth) and the usages of what will be deleted

limits.text: StyleSheet is not watched by the data contract: read it back with get. Deleting a screen must handle navigation consumers and the module DefaultScreen (appears with an empty path in the refusal).
Reordering or inserting sibling widgets can trip the strict merge equivalence gate on DisplayOrder (outcome uncertain: never retry, read the receipt).

capabilities.guidance: Renaming a screen or block rewrites references by key; CSS classes, captions and hand-written deep links stay as text.

capabilities.title: Theme CSS (three halves) and screen/block stylesheets
capabilities.summary: `set StyleSheet` on a theme writes the author half (Theme Editor CSS is a separate half; the effective sheet is generated + author); screens and blocks have their own StyleSheet.

route.operation: get ITheme:X (three halves) then set StyleSheet with the whole author text

alternatives.when: the CSS belongs to a fragment: `<style>` is installed under the fragment class

limits.text: Writing StyleSheet replaces the author CSS: read the three halves first to append. A CSS-only feature must still carry an element stamped by the snapshot author or the manifest gate refuses (audit T1 CSS episode).

capabilities.title: Scripts (JS files), resources and required scripts
capabilities.summary: IScript with JavaScript, IResource with TargetDirectory/DeployAction, and `RequiredScripts` of a screen; RuntimePath is derived and follows renames.

route.operation: create IScript|IResource; set JavaScript/TargetDirectory/DeployAction; link screen RequiredScripts

limits.text: ResourceContent is read-only in the Model API V1 (binary content cannot be written by jobs); write TargetDirectory after DeployAction or the platform discards it. Module images (IImage) are not created by jobs.

capabilities.title: Emails, popovers and aggregate metadata
capabilities.summary: IMobileEmail lives in the Emails UI flow (EmailTheme); IPopover is born complete (TopContent/BottomContent); ITextMetadata hangs on a screen aggregate with managedBy.

route.operation: create IMobileEmail in IMobileFlow:Emails; create IPopover; ISendEmailNode in a server action

capabilities.title: Rename with propagation report
capabilities.summary: `rename` refuses name clashes and returns consumers and expressionsRewritten; the platform rewrites what is model (expressions, SQL, aggregates, node names), not literals, descriptions, CSS or hand-written URLs.

route.operation: {"op":"rename","target":"IServerAction:Old","name":"New"} then get/dump the expressions that cite it

limits.text: Renaming an exposed REST method rewrites its public URL; renaming a static entity record is `set Identifier`; IEvent/ISystemEvent/IBlockEvent renames are refused or silently ignored on ODC.

capabilities.title: Repoint every consumer (replace)
capabilities.summary: `replace from to` makes every consumer of `from` point at `to` (the Studio's ReplaceReferences); afterwards the old element has no consumers and `delete` needs no force.

limits.text: Different kinds need force and usually break Verify; literals, descriptions, URLs and CSS never propagate.

capabilities.title: Duplicate (Ctrl+D) an element
capabilities.summary: `duplicate` copies into the same parent at the end, with the platform suffix and without consumers; internal references follow the copy.

limits.text: A duplicated action is UnusedAction until something calls it: declare the warning or repoint a consumer.

capabilities.title: Reorder inside the same parent
capabilities.summary: `move` reorders attributes, widgets, parameters or variables inside the same parent (first/last/before/after) or positions a flow node (x/y); with `into` it changes the parent (folder for top-level elements, key kept; the Studio's own move otherwise: new key, consumers rebound). It returns the resulting order.

alternatives.when: a widget must change parent: C# features use IModelServices.MoveObject (strict-merge proof per feature)

capabilities.title: Delete with consumer check (usages first)
capabilities.summary: `delete` refuses while real consumers exist and names each one by path; derived usages (aggregate attribute lists, example record values) do not count; `force` breaks them (brokenConsumers). Use `usages` first and repoint or remove the consumers.

limits.text: Deleting sweeps down (children), never up: variables that only fed the deleted element stay as orphans. To delete a node in the middle of a flow relink the predecessor first.

capabilities.title: Read an application capture: map, elements, properties, usages
capabilities.summary: Read-only reader over a capture (.oml, reused by hash) or the open module: module map, `kind`/`name`/`text` queries with paging, a path or @key subtree with depth, `--usages` for consumers, `--select` for up to 32 paths in one call, `budget` for the inline size (the full JSON is always written to `out`).

route.operation: odc inspect <capture.oml> --kind ServerEntity --max 50 --properties Name; odc inspect <capture.oml> "MobileScreen:Home" --depth 4; --usages

limits.text: Limits are in the tool schema: select <= 32, depth <= 12, max <= 500, budget 2000..200000; ok=true means the query ran, check notices/kindObserved/searchComplete/omissions before treating a result as complete. Kinds are interface names without the leading I (MobileScreen, ServerAction, MobileBlockSignature...).

capabilities.guidance: Reuse the same capture between pages; after a Studio change take a new capture. Facade proof: platforms/odc/facade/tests/reading.test.mjs.

capabilities.title: Deliver a job to the open module directly
capabilities.summary: `studio_deliver {feature, module, job, owners, changes}`, directly: captures the open module as it is now, applies the job privately on that capture, prepares the manifest (no new errors or warnings; a change against the capture, read element by element; stamps only name the author), then the native merge (strictlyEqual; the merge itself proves the base and the preview conditions), refusing before any change. Publishes in the same call only with publish:true, after a clean merge, with the user's words (authorize) or a standing grant. `ssam job --lane odc <job>` applies the job on the lane fixture (Verify + expected messages, delivers nothing) only when the person asks for a headless proof.

alternatives.when: the change cannot be expressed as a job (new module, producer dependency, reparenting, pattern widgets from a reference)

limits.text: The base of a job is the fixture or `job:<name>`; for delivery the facade supplies the snapshot as base. A job with expectValid:false is never deliverable. The kernel CLI must report flowLayoutEngine anvil-d4d8ece or delivery refuses.

Refusal vocabulary: base_drift (new snapshot and build), candidate_validation (fix the job), equivalence (merge pending in the Studio, never repeat), known_losses (merged except the named defaults; deliver the repair the continuation names), studio_busy (dismiss the dialog by caption), uncertain (read receipt.json / last-error.json / journal; never retry).

capabilities.guidance: Headless proof is not delivery evidence; a merge receipt with merged=true and strictlyEqual=true is.

capabilities.title: C# feature route (Authoring primitives) for what jobs cannot express
capabilities.summary: An IFeature in platforms/odc/studio/builder/features using Authoring/AuthoringData/AuthoringUi/AuthoringMisc/AuthoringRest primitives and ModelPath; `odc build list` shows the registered features; `odc build <feature> <base.oml> <sha> <dir> --smoke` proves headless; `odc deliver <feature>` runs the same gates as jobs. Required for: new module (INewModule + create), AddDependency with --producer, IModelServices.MoveObject reparenting, widgets from a reference WidgetDefinition, native Copy of producer nodes.

route.operation: write features/<Name>.cs (copy LabScreen.cs / LabBlock.cs / LabAction.cs), dotnet build studio/builder, odc build list, odc deliver <feature> --until preview

alternatives.when: a job can express the change: jobs are proven on the fixture and need no C# compile

limits.text: Live-merged proofs of the feature route live in platforms/odc/lab/<dir>/evidence/receipt.json (merged/strictlyEqual) of the operational checkout; they are not part of this index. The builder refuses any new warning; Caption replaces the default button text; Icon needs weight; the native Button Group cannot be authored; Data Actions take no inputs.

capabilities.guidance: Model API reference for C#: platforms/odc/docs/model-api/INDEX.md (reflection, ODC Studio version recorded there).

capabilities.title: Authorize and publish (user's own words)
capabilities.summary: After a merge receipt, `odc studio authorize <manifest> publish "<the user's own words>"` records the authorization and `odc studio publish <manifest> --wait` publishes natively and downloads the revision for comparison. Publication is never automatic and never retried after an uncertain result.

route.operation: studio_authorize {manifest, kind:"publish", text} then studio_publish {manifest, wait:true}

depends.unless: the merge receipt came from the feature route (deliver.feature): publication needs a merge receipt, whichever route produced it

limits.text: The text must be the user's words, quoted, not a paraphrase; outcome `MergeAndPublish` in a merge receipt is a native label and does not mean a publication happened (publishInvoked says).

On ODC processes are Workflow assets edited in the ODC Portal, not elements of the module model; no job or feature creates them.

unavailable.reason: IRestClient.Username/Password accept writes but Verify rejects them as errors on ODC; only the authentication mode stays in the model.

The ODC kernel has no headless producer import (ImportReference throws NotSupported): the `reference` verb is O11-only; on ODC references are refreshed live by the bridge (studio_refresh_references) or added by a C# feature with --producer.
unavailable.evidence: kernel/src/Anvil.Core.Odc/Adapters.ODC/README.md; index: no ODC job uses op reference
